title: Assert in pgstat_report_stat() fails when a backend shuts down with stats pending
body: I am running PostgreSQL 16.0 on Ubuntu 22.04. While looping check-world on a slow device, all tests passed, but the system journal reported a postgres crash. I reproduced it in the recovery-test logs: a walsender hit Assert("!pgStatLocal.shmem->is_shutdown") in pgstat_report_stat() during shutdown. The stack trace reaches pgstat_report_stat() through shmem_exit(). It appears when the backend still has pending statistics after statistics shutdown; with no pending entries, pgstat_report_stats() returns before the assertion. Making pgstat_flush_pending_entries() randomly leave a nowait entry unflushed reproduces the assertion easily while t/012_subtransactions.pl still reports PASS.

symptoms_visible: My check-world run reports that every test passed, but the system journal and recovery-test log contain a postgres crash.
The log shows a walsender failing Assert("!pgStatLocal.shmem->is_shutdown") in pgstat_report_stat() during process exit.
When I randomly leave a nowait statistics entry unflushed, t/012_subtransactions.pl still says PASS but its primary log contains the assertion trap.
N0.label: N0 shutdown assertion reported and reproduced

symptoms_visible: I found the same walsender assertion in a REL_17_STABLE buildfarm recovery-test log.
That run also reported fewer pg_stat_statements rows than the test expected.
N1.label: N1 stable-branch recurrence established

symptoms_visible: The unpatched recovery-test log can still contain the walsender shutdown assertion even when the test command reports success.
N2.label: N2 stable-branch scoped patch proposed

symptoms_visible: With the candidate patch applied, my forced recovery test passes without the shutdown assertion appearing.
Using PostgreSQL's PRNG for the forced-flush test gives varying runs rather than the same random sequence I observed on macOS.
N3.label: N3 candidate patch verified

symptoms_visible: The forced shutdown test completes without a walsender assertion when run with the verified patch.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Has the same assertion appeared in another run or supported branch?
Do you have another log showing whether this is limited to PostgreSQL 16?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found the same failure in a REL_17_STABLE buildfarm recovery run. Its primary log shows a walsender releasing a replication slot and then failing the same !pgStatLocal.shmem->is_shutdown assertion.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it outside my locally modified PostgreSQL 16 tree, and no unmodified build has shown the assertion.
The same assertion appeared in another PostgreSQL 16 recovery run rather than REL_17_STABLE.

question_patterns: What did the surrounding buildfarm test observe when the assertion occurred?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The recovery test expected CREATE, DELETE, INSERT, SELECT and UPDATE rows in pg_stat_statements, but it got only CREATE and SELECT, with CREATE marked false.

edges.comment: Thread c0, posted by the original reporter: the reporter identified a later buildfarm recurrence on REL_17_STABLE and quoted its raw assertion and test output. This is the same walsender shutdown problem, not a different participant's deployment.

solution.intent: Use a narrow stable-branch correction rather than backpatching the newer shutdown-sequencing redesign: tolerate pending statistics during WAL-sender shutdown while retaining the assertion for other backend types, and make the shutdown hook safely handle remaining WAL-sender statistics.
solution.concrete_example: For the supported stable branches, lift the shutdown assertion only for WAL senders and adjust pgstat_shutdown_hook so that statistics still present during WAL-sender exit are handled safely. Avoid wholesale backpatching of the newer shutdown-sequence rework.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers concluded that the broad newer shutdown-ordering change was too invasive for stable branches. Their accepted design was to relax the invariant only for WAL senders and add shutdown-hook handling for statistics that can remain there.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c4: participant2 initially suggested backpatching an equivalent of a newer change, but participants2 and3 then agreed that this was too invasive. Participant3 supplied the narrower 15~17 patch that became the accepted fix.

question_patterns: Can you apply the candidate patch, rerun your forced recovery-test reproducer, and report whether the assertion still appears?
Please test the proposed patch with the same shutdown workload and tell me what appears in the log.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The patch works for me test-wise. With it applied, the forced recovery test passes and I do not get the assertion.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same walsender assertion still appears with the candidate patch applied.
The patched test passes on repeated runs, although the number of forced flush failures varies between runs.

question_patterns: Is there any adjustment needed to make the forced-failure reproducer reliable across platforms?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used pg_prng_double(&pg_global_prng_state) for the one-in-ten forced failure. rand() gave me the same sequence on macOS each run, while on Linux I saw different sequences.

question_patterns: Was the forced test also checked against both the unpatched and patched code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The forced test reproduces the failure before the patch and runs without it after the patch.

edges.comment: Thread c5-c6: the reporter supplied the pg_prng-based variant and confirmed that participant3's candidate patch worked. Participant3 separately stated that the failure reproduced before the patch and disappeared afterward. The maintainer result is folded into the simulated user side as relayed evidence, while the candidate-patch success is the reporter's own test.

solution.intent: Apply the verified narrow stable-branch fix: permit WAL senders to reach statistics shutdown with entries still pending, safely deal with those entries in pgstat_shutdown_hook, and preserve the shutdown assertion for other backend processes.
solution.concrete_example: Ship the tested patch for the affected stable branches. It was applied as 4801610f7c66 in the v15~17 range after the reporter's forced-shutdown test passed.

edges.comment: Thread c7: participant3 applied the same scoped patch to v15~17 after the reporter and maintainer verified the forced reproducer. Later discussion in c8-c10 only concerns which equivalent WAL-sender identification helper/include to use and does not change the accepted diagnosis or fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: a WAL sender can still have pending statistics when shared statistics shutdown has already been marked complete, so its exit-time pgstat_report_stat() call reaches an assertion whose invariant is not valid for that shutdown ordering.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the walsender stack trace, the pending-entry reproducer, and the recurrence on a stable-branch buildfarm run.

The fix must be narrowly scoped to WAL senders: relax the shutdown assertion for that process type, retain it for other backends, and safely handle remaining WAL-sender statistics in pgstat_shutdown_hook.
Must not recommend wholesale backpatching of the newer shutdown-sequence redesign as the stable-branch fix; maintainers considered that approach too invasive.
Must use the reporter's successful candidate-patch run with the forced reproducer as verification before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: PostgreSQL developer and test-infrastructure contributor who can read backend shutdown code, modify C sources to create a probabilistic reproducer, inspect stack traces, and test patches across platforms.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, concise, and evidence-driven; includes exact assertions, commands, code snippets, and raw test output, then promptly verifies proposed patches.
